title: Can I BEAT King of the Bridge?
summary: The creator plays the indie game King of the Bridge. A small character must cross a bridge guarded by a riddle-loving troll who instead challenges him to 'the 11th edition of Advanced Troll Chess'. A rule book on the right lists numbered rules, many hidden until they are 'unlocked' (with a gong sound) when the troll uses them. The troll cheats; the player presses Space to enter accusation mode, clicks the offending piece and the rule page it violated. A correct accusation ('Officer, arrest him') lets the player cheat that turn as payback; a false accusation forfeits your turn and lets the troll cheat as revenge. Losing your king ends the game; when the troll's king dies it passes its crown to another piece. He loses several attempts (retrying), learns rules like pawns moving sideways/backwards, pawns not capturing normally, slippery squares that knock pieces over, the board flipping, bishops working 'out of town', then wins by out-waiting the troll with boring play and catching every cheat.
rules: Rule 00: if you catch the other colour cheating (correct accusation), you may cheat during your turn as payback.
Rule 1: if you falsely accuse, your turn is forfeited and the other side may cheat as revenge.
Rule 2: you may only move your own coloured pieces.

Rule 4: pawns are 'small-minded': can step side to side (and pawns can also move backwards per a later rule); pawns can't capture in the normal way (pawn captures differ - 'pawns can't capture' accusation); special pawn target squares.
Rule 7: 'Horse guy' (knight) can also move in an extra four-direction pattern; he is 'troubled' (must trot/canter/gallop).
Rule 9: only the knight can jump over other pieces.
Rule 10: if the white (player's) king dies, black wins.
Rule 11: if the black (troll's) king dies, the crown is handed to another black piece (royal guard transfer).
Rule 12: 'Crown guy' (king) can do as he pleases but is lazy - limited move pattern.
Rule 13: bishop travels in an X (diagonals).
Rule 14: towers (rooks) can't normally move but in this world can move a special way.
Rule 16+: further rules unlock during play.
Rule 24: do not walk in each other's shoes (pieces can't share/occupy each other's... cryptic).
Rule 25: no pieces can move outside the board unless they work 'out of town' (only bishops may leave the board).
Some tiles are slippery: a piece stepping on them falls over and must be clicked to stand up (costs a move); a queen slipping flips the board.
The queen must not capture the king ('royal affair').
Accusation flow: press Space, click the suspected piece, then click the rule page violated, confirm.
win_condition: Eliminate the troll's pieces (king captures just transfer the crown) to cross the bridge.
